component.name: Scour
component.summary: File index and search for a machine with millions of files

description.p: Scour keeps every file and folder of the volumes it is given in an index of its own, updates that index as the filesystem changes, and answers searches from it in milliseconds. It walks the filesystem once rather than on every query. It depends on no external search engine and no database, and by default it indexes the home directory.

One service holds the index and four interfaces connect to it over a local socket, sharing its settings: a command line, a native window, a page served to the browser, and a full-screen terminal interface. The menu entry opens whichever of them was last switched to.

Searching is case-insensitive. Whitespace means AND, a vertical bar means OR, an exclamation mark negates, quotes enclose a phrase, and the asterisk and question mark are wildcards. A term of the form field:value restricts a field — among them the extension, the size, the date modified, the kind of file, and the directory a result must be under. Parsing does not fail: an unrecognised field is searched for as text, and the explain command shows how a query was read.
The same index is exposed to language models through a Model Context Protocol server with eleven read-only tools, each of which bounds its answer and reports when it was truncated.
This is an alpha release. The index format may change between releases.

description.p: The report draws what it measures in every face; the keyboard shortcut is set from inside Scour; a face starts the service itself; one service instance per account; packages for Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora.
Columns, query rails, and a service that costs less to run.
